2608.25071.title: HealthBench-Psych: A Mental Health Subset of OpenAI's HealthBench
2608.25071.paper_summary: General-purpose health benchmarks increasingly anchor claims about LLM medical performance, but they are not always resolved by clinical specialty, making domain-specific performance hard to isolate. Mental health is of acute public-health concern as millions of people turn to LLMs for psychological support, and most existing evaluations are bespoke academic benchmarks that are difficult to integrate into developer workflows. We introduce HealthBench-Psych and HealthBench-Psych-Hard. We screened HealthBench's 5,000 physician-rubric conversations for mental-health relevance with a transparent LLM-applied rubric, then validated the subset through two rounds of blinded clinician review with concealed known-exclude controls, yielding 610 conversations (12.2% of the corpus). Evaluating 20 frontier and open models under a cross-vendor panel of three LLM judges, we find a statistically tied frontier cluster, measurable refusal behavior in two models, and near-identical rankings across judges ($τ\ge 0.92$). We release the subset, pipeline, model responses, grades, and analysis code as a reusable resource.
2608.25071.paper_summary_zh: 一般用途的健康基準越來越多地成為有關大型語言模型（LLM）醫療表現的主張基礎，但它們並不總是依據臨床專業來解決，使得特定領域的表現難以孤立。心理健康是當前公共健康的重大關注，因為數百萬人轉向LLM尋求心理支持，而現有的大多數評估都是定制的學術基準，難以整合進開發者的工作流程。我們推出了HealthBench-Psych和HealthBench-Psych-Hard。我們使用透明的LLM應用標準篩選了HealthBench的5,000個醫生評分對話，以確定其心理健康相關性，然後通過兩輪盲法臨床醫生審查進行驗證，並隱藏已知排除控制，最終獲得610個對話（佔語料庫的12.2%）。在三位LLM評審的跨供應商小組下評估20個前沿和開放模型，我們發現一個統計上相當的前沿集群，兩個模型中可測量的拒絕行為，以及評審之間幾乎相同的排名（$τ\ge 0.92$）。我們將這個子集、管道、模型回應、評分和分析代碼作為可重用資源發布。
